chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Shurayh, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Amr ibn Nahik, from Salam al-Makki, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who was called Shaybah al-Hudhali, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I am an old man whose age has advanced and my strength has weakened to perform the deeds I had accustomed myself to, namely prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and striving. So teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a phrase that Allah will benefit me with, and lighten the burden for me, O Messenger of Allah.'

He said to him, 'Repeat.' So he repeated it three times. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Around you, every tree and every clod of earth is weeping out of mercy for you.'

So when you have prayed the morning prayer, say ten times: 'Glory be to Allah the Great, and to Him be praise. There is no power and no strength except with Allah the Exalted, the Great.' For indeed, Allah will cure you thereby from blindness, insanity, leprosy, poverty, and old age.'

He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, this is for the world, so what is for the Hereafter?' He said, 'You say after every prayer: 'O Allah, guide me from Yourself, and pour upon me from Your grace, and spread upon me from Your mercy, and send down upon me from Your blessings.'
He said, So he grasped them with his hand, then departed. And a man said to Ibn Abbas, 'How firmly your uncle grasped them!'

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Indeed, if he fulfills them on the Day of Resurrection, not having missed any deliberately, Allah will open for him eight gates of the gates of Paradise, from whichever he wishes.'

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْ: Glory be to Allah the Great and to Him be praise
key_terms.شَيْبَةُ اَلْهُذَيْلِ: Shaybah al-Hudhali, the name of the man who approached the Prophet
key_terms.لاَ حَوْلَ وَ لاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّ: There is no power and no strength except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What specific supplication did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) teach an elderly man to compensate for his weakened ability to perform prayers and fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia emphasis on *taysir* (ease) for the elderly, where the Prophet prescribes specific dhikr to compensate for physical decline. The detailed narration, including Ibn Abbas’s observation of the Prophet grasping the supplications, underscores the spiritual weight of these specific formulas, linking worldly protection from ailments like blindness and poverty with the eschatological reward of entering Paradise through any of its eight gates.
